correctness.rationale: For all integer n≥2 and all 0<p≤1, contraction triangle inequality bounds by ℓ1 coefficient discrepancy; one ℓ∞ unilateral shift with sign vector attains this bound exactly. Normalized probability masses give the finite formula; compact-uniform Riemann-sum convergence yields the limiting piecewise objective. Its derivative is strictly single-crossing by a monotone e^λ log(λ)/λ² ratio; initial-segment mass tests rule out minimizers with np→0 or np→∞, giving convergence of every finite minimizer to the unique asymptotic λ. Independent rational finite checks and numeric scaling tests corroborate but do not replace proof. The coefficient formula is for real or complex Banach contractions, no hidden spectral assumptions.

value.rationale: The Cesàro average of operator iterates and Abel resolvent are canonical summability schemes. The minimax penalty under only the contraction assumption determines whether one discount can replace one finite uniform averaging window uniformly; the strict positive obstruction and exactly optimized discount answer a natural stability/approximation question. Its shift extremizer and finite candidate rule give constructive operational interpretation beyond ordinary pointwise Tauberian equivalence. Conventional p=1/n has a quantitatively larger limiting loss, making the sharp rate substantive.
